heading: 4 steps
steps: Download all statements since the card was opened (or last 2–3 years)
Add up every purchase and cash withdrawal
Subtract every payment and refund you made
What's left = your principal (no interest, fees or GST)

Different banks never combine — each bank settles only its own dues
Same bank, many cards or loans: ask for ONE letter covering all of them

title: Lok Adalat Notice — The Real Picture
sub: Is attending compulsory? What happens if you don't go? How to use it well.

topic: "I got a Lok Adalat notice — will they arrest me if I don't go?"

heading: What Lok Adalat really is
items: A settlement meeting — not a regular court case
Attending is voluntary — no arrest, no fine for not going
No award without YOUR consent — both sides must agree
If you skip, the bank may later file a regular case
If you agree, the award is final — there is no appeal

left.title: Worth going if…
items: You can arrange some money now
You want to close the account
Offers here are often lower

right.title: It's okay to skip if…
items: You have no money right now
You don't want to sign under pressure
Send a written reply to the bank instead

heading: If you go — checklist
items: Carry ID proof, the notice and your statements
Know your principal — negotiate from it
Ask for instalments if you can't pay at once
Read the award: amount, dates, 'full and final'
Get a certified copy of the award
Pay only to the bank's official account

title: ₹20 Lakh & ₹25 Lakh — DRT, Auction, Wilful Defaulter
sub: When can property really be auctioned? What the numbers mean.

heading: The ₹20 lakh line — DRT
source: Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993 — Sec 1(4)
items: Debts Recovery Tribunal (DRT) handles only dues of ₹20 lakh or more
Counted per bank — NOT your total across all banks
Below ₹20 lakh: civil court, arbitration or Lok Adalat
Property can be attached / auctioned only after a decree or recovery certificate
An agent can never auction or seize anything

left.title: SARFAESI auction
items: Only for SECURED loans (home, property)
Bank gives 60-day notice, then can take possession
Needs a registered charge on the asset

right.title: Credit card
items: UNSECURED — SARFAESI does not apply
Bank must first win a case (court / DRT)
Only then can any property be attached

heading: Examples
note: DRT is only a forum — even there, you get notice and a chance to defend.
rows: No — every bank is below ₹20 lakh

heading: The ₹25 lakh line — 'wilful defaulter'
source: RBI Master Direction on Wilful Defaulters, 2024
items: Applies only when ₹25 lakh or more is outstanding
AND the default is wilful — could pay but didn't, or misused the money
Genuine hardship (job loss, illness) is not wilful default
Keep proof of hardship; deal honestly and in writing

can: Charge interest & late fees (as per terms)
Call & remind you (8 AM – 7 PM only)
Set-off dues from your account in the SAME bank
Go to court / arbitration / Lok Adalat
cannot: Seize property without a court order
Call before 8 AM or after 7 PM
Threaten, abuse or shame you publicly
Tell your relatives, friends or office about your debt
Charge over-limit fees without your consent

headline: Card default is a CIVIL matter
sub: Not a crime. No FIR, no arrest — just for not paying.

exceptions.text: A cheque you gave bounces (Sec 138, NI Act)
Bank-account auto-debit / NACH bounces (Sec 25, PSS Act)
Fraud from day one — fake documents / identity

Calls to family, friends, office, references

pairs: "Police will arrest you"
Non-payment alone is civil. No arrest, no FIR.
"Arrest warrant issued"
Only a COURT issues warrants — after a proper summons, not WhatsApp.
"We'll seize your house today"
Agents have zero such power. Only a court decree & process.
"We'll stop your salary"
Only a court order can. Agents can't shame you to your employer.
"Pay something now, case closes"
Small payments close nothing. Pay only to the bank's official account, with a written plan.

heading: Recovery agent rules
source: RBI circular, 12 Aug 2022 · Outsourcing & Fair Practices directions
items: No calls before 8 AM or after 7 PM
No intimidation, abuse, threats or public humiliation
No intrusion into privacy of family, friends, referees
No anonymous / threatening calls or abusive social-media messages
No false or misleading statements
The BANK is responsible for its agents' conduct

heading: Credit card rules
source: RBI Master Direction — Credit & Debit Cards (Issuance and Conduct), 2022
items: No late fee or 'past due' reporting until 3 days after due date
No interest on unpaid fees & charges (no capitalisation)
No over-limit charges without your explicit consent
Minimum due must not make the debt keep growing
After settlement: bank must update CIBIL within 30 days

title: Notices Decoded — Which One Is Serious?
sub: WhatsApp 'notice', lawyer's notice, arbitration, court summons, cheque bounce.

heading: Five kinds of 'notice'
note: When in doubt, show it to an advocate or your nearest free Legal Services Authority.

heading: Cheque bounce / NACH notice
source: NI Act Sec 138 · PSS Act Sec 25
items: Comes only if a cheque or bank auto-debit you gave has bounced
This one is criminal — you get 15 days after the notice
Pay or reply within the time; meet an advocate immediately

heading: Arbitration — know this
source: Arbitration & Conciliation Act · Supreme Court, Perkins Eastman (2019)
items: An arbitration award can be enforced like a court decree
An arbitrator appointed by one side alone is not valid
Reply in writing and raise your objection early
Ignoring it can lead to an award in your absence

items.text: Court summons: court name, case number, seal & signature
Check the case number on eCourts: services.ecourts.gov.in
Lawyer's notice: letterhead with enrolment number & address
Free legal help: your District Legal Services Authority

pairs: Will I go to jail?
No — not for non-payment. Only a bounced cheque / NACH or fraud is criminal.
Can they freeze my bank accounts?
Other banks: only with a court order. Same bank: set-off possible.
Can they call my office?
They must not disclose your debt to your employer or colleagues.
Does the debt vanish after 7 years?
No. Credit report history fades; the bank's claim & case risk don't simply vanish.
Can I settle in instalments?
Often yes — 2 to 6 parts. Get the letter first.
Will my home loan / other EMIs be affected?
They continue normally if you keep paying them. New loans get hard.
Can I travel abroad?
Card default alone doesn't stop travel. But never ignore court summons.
Can an agent take my bike or phone?
No. Agents have no power to take anything.
After settlement, can they ask again?
Not if you have a proper 'full and final' letter + NOC.
Pay full or settle?
If you can, pay in full — 'Closed' is far better than 'Settled'.
Will I get a card again?
Yes, after a clean record — start small, e.g. a secured card.

title: 12 More Questions People Ask
sub: ARC, other accounts, references, recording calls, jobs, passport, CIBIL errors…

pairs: My debt was sold to an ARC — now what?
Same debt, new owner — RBI rules still apply. Ask for the assignment letter; settle only with them, in writing.
Can they debit my account in another bank?
Only if you gave a mandate (NACH / standing instruction). Cancel old mandates.
They're calling my friends and references!
They may try to trace you, but must not reveal your debt or harass them. Complain.
Can I record recovery calls?
Recording your own calls as evidence is generally fine. Keep them safe.
Will calls stop after I settle?
They should. If calls continue after the NOC, complain to the bank and RBI.
Can default affect my job?
Some employers (banks, finance) check credit reports. Otherwise, usually not.
Passport or visa problems?
Card default alone doesn't affect your passport. Look-out circulars are for serious fraud or huge cases.
My card had 'credit shield' insurance?
Check it — it may cover death, disability or job loss.
Should I take a personal loan to pay cards?
Only if the rate is much lower, EMI is affordable, and you stop using cards. Never app loans.
Can I convert my card dues into EMI?
Yes — ask BEFORE default. It's much cheaper than revolving.
CIBIL still wrong after settlement?
Dispute with CIBIL & the bank. Not fixed in 30 days → ₹100/day compensation (RBI).
Can I settle while my card is still regular?
Usually no — ask for an EMI plan or restructuring instead.

heading: 7-step action plan
steps: Stop using the card — stop rotation
List every debt: balance, min. due, due date, rate
Protect essentials: rent, food, medicine, auto-debit EMIs
E-mail the bank early: EMI conversion / restructuring
Explain your hardship honestly — in writing
Plan a lump sum for settlement
Never take app loans to pay card dues

heading: Settlement checklist
items: Negotiate on the principal — in writing, with the bank
Get the settlement letter on bank letterhead BEFORE paying
Letter must show amount, account no. & 'full and final settlement'
Pay ONLY to the bank's official account / link — never agent UPI or cash

heading: 'Settled' is not 'Closed'
items: 'Settled' = you paid less than owed → lenders see it as negative
Later, pay the waived amount → status can become 'Closed'
Rebuild: on-time payments, low usage, time
